pr.title: Add partial refunds to the payments API
pr.body: Adds partial refunds behind the `partialRefunds` flag. See the ReviewHub briefing for decisions, validation and rollout.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,12 @@
+CREATE TABLE refunds (
+  id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
+  order_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id),
+  amount_cents BIGINT NOT NULL CHECK (amount_cents > 0),
+  currency CHAR(3) NOT NULL,
+  reason TEXT,
+  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
+);
+
+CREATE INDEX refunds_order_id_idx ON refunds(order_id);
+
+ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN refunded_amount BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;

@@ -14,2 +14,5 @@
   "orders.notFound": "Order not found",
+  "refunds.amountExceedsRemaining": "The refund is larger than the amount left to refund.",
+  "refunds.orderNotCaptured": "Only paid orders can be refunded.",
+  "refunds.idempotencyKeyRequired": "Send an Idempotency-Key header with every refund request.",
   "orders.shipped": "Order shipped"

@@ -0,0 +1,20 @@
+# Refunds
+
+Create a full or partial refund for a captured order.
+
+## `POST /orders/:orderId/refunds`
+
+| Header            | Required | Description                                 |
+| ----------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------- |
+| `Idempotency-Key` | yes      | Retries with the same key return the same refund. |
+
+```json
+{ "amount": { "cents": 2500, "currency": "EUR" }, "reason": "Damaged item" }
+```
+
+### Responses
+
+- `201` the refund was created
+- `404` the order does not exist
+- `409` the order is not captured, or the amount exceeds what is left to refund
+- `422` the request body is invalid

@@ -0,0 +1,11 @@
+// Vitest Snapshot v1
+
+exports[`createRefund > refunds part of a captured order 1`] = `
+{
+  "amount_cents": 2500,
+  "currency": "EUR",
+  "id": 1,
+  "order_id": 1,
+  "reason": null,
+}
+`;

prompt.original: Add support for partial refunds to the payments API. Merchants should be able to refund part of an order via `PUT /refunds/:orderId` with an amount. Make sure we never refund more than was captured, and put it behind a feature flag. Use our existing money helpers.
followUps: Also make sure retries from the merchant's side don't create duplicate refunds.

data.summary: Adds `POST /orders/:orderId/refunds` behind the `partialRefunds` flag. A refund is stored in a new `refunds` table, the order's `refunded_amount` is updated in the same transaction, and the refund is spread over the order's line items for the existing `refund.created` worker. Retries are de-duplicated with an `Idempotency-Key` header.

deviations.title: Endpoint is `POST /orders/:orderId/refunds`, not `PUT /refunds/:orderId`
deviations.delivered: `POST /orders/:orderId/refunds` that creates a new refund resource on each call.
deviations.reason: An order can now have several partial refunds, so each call creates a resource rather than replacing one. `PUT` keyed by order id would make a second partial refund overwrite the first. Retry safety comes from the `Idempotency-Key` header instead.

deviations.title: Changed rounding in the shared `percentOf` helper
deviations.delivered: `percentOf` now uses banker's rounding (half to even) instead of `Math.round`.
deviations.reason: Half-up rounding over many line items made allocated parts drift from the refund total by a cent. The new `allocate` helper needs consistent rounding, so I changed `percentOf` to match. This also affects the existing callers of `percentOf` (discounts and tax).

decisions.title: Idempotency keys are stored in Redis with a 24 hour TTL
decisions.context: The follow-up asked that merchant retries never create duplicate refunds. The prompt didn't say where to remember keys or for how long.
decisions.chosen: Cache the created refund in Redis under the idempotency key for 24 hours.
decisions.rationale: Redis is already a dependency, lookups are cheap, and 24 hours matches the retry window of our SDKs.

alternatives.title: Unique constraint in Postgres
alternatives.description: Store `idempotency_key` on the `refunds` row with a unique index on `(merchant_id, idempotency_key)`.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Durable and transactional: survives a Redis flush and cannot race. Needs one more column and index in the migration.
alternatives.prompt: Replace the Redis-based idempotency in src/payments/refunds.ts with a unique index on refunds(merchant_id, idempotency_key). Add the column to the migration, insert inside the existing transaction, and on a unique violation return the existing refund. Remove the Redis calls and update the tests.

alternatives.title: Shared idempotency middleware
alternatives.description: Handle the `Idempotency-Key` header in an Express middleware for all mutating endpoints.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Reusable across endpoints, but a larger change than this PR asked for.

decisions.title: Partial refunds are spread over line items proportionally
decisions.context: The downstream `refund.created` worker needs per-line-item amounts for tax reporting. The prompt only specified a total amount.
decisions.chosen: Split the amount proportionally by line item value, using the largest-remainder method so parts always add up.
decisions.rationale: It's predictable and needs no extra input from merchants.

alternatives.title: Let merchants specify line items
alternatives.description: Accept an optional `lineItems` array in the request body.
alternatives.tradeoffs: More accurate for item-level returns, but a bigger API surface to document and validate.
alternatives.prompt: Extend POST /orders/:orderId/refunds to accept an optional lineItems array of { lineItemId, cents }. Validate that it sums to amount.cents and fall back to proportional allocation when it's missing.

decisions.title: Business rule violations return 409
decisions.context: Refunding more than is left, or refunding an uncaptured order, isn't a malformed request.
decisions.chosen: Return 409 Conflict with an error code. 422 is reserved for invalid bodies.
decisions.rationale: Matches how the orders API already reports state conflicts.

alternatives.title: 422 for everything
alternatives.description: Use 422 for both validation and business-rule errors.

data.summary: One critical and two high findings in the new refund path. The SQL injection and missing ownership check together let any merchant refund any order. Fix both before merging.

findings.title: SQL injection through orderId
findings.description: `orderId` comes straight from the URL and is interpolated into the SQL string. A request to `/orders/1' OR '1'='1/refunds` changes the query.

suggestion.explanation: Use a parameterized query so the driver escapes the value.
suggestion.prompt: In src/payments/refunds.ts, replace the interpolated SQL in createRefund with a parameterized query. Then search src/ for other template-literal SQL passed to db.one, db.many or db.query and fix those the same way.

findings.title: Merchants can refund orders that belong to other merchants
findings.description: `requireMerchant` authenticates the caller, but nothing checks that the order belongs to that merchant. Any merchant who can guess an order id can refund it.

suggestion.explanation: Pass the authenticated merchant through and filter the order lookup by it, so foreign orders look the same as missing ones (404).
suggestion.prompt: Add a required merchantId to RefundRequest in src/payments/refunds.ts and filter the order lookup with `AND merchant_id = $2`. Pass req.merchant.id from the route. Add a test showing a merchant gets 404 for another merchant's order.

findings.title: Concurrent refunds can exceed the captured amount
findings.description: The remaining amount is checked before the transaction starts, and the update writes an absolute value. Two parallel requests can both pass the check, and the second write overwrites the first.

suggestion.explanation: Lock the order row inside the transaction (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`), check the remaining amount there, and update with `refunded_amount = refunded_amount + $1`.
suggestion.prompt: In src/payments/refunds.ts, move the order lookup and the remaining-amount check inside db.transaction and lock the row with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE. Update refunded_amount relative to its current value. Add an integration test that fires two refunds in parallel and asserts only one succeeds when together they exceed the captured amount.

findings.title: Idempotency keys aren't scoped to the merchant
findings.description: The Redis key only contains the client-supplied idempotency key. If two merchants send the same key, the second gets the first merchant's refund back, including its order id and amount.

suggestion.explanation: Prefix the key with the merchant id (once it's passed in, see the ownership finding).

findings.title: Flag-off responses reveal the endpoint exists
findings.description: The 404 is returned after `requireMerchant`, so unauthenticated callers get 401 and can tell the route exists. Low impact while the flag is temporary.

suggestion.explanation: Check the flag when mounting the router instead of inside the handler.
